validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real and correctly classified. This is the Tioga–Elkhorn Creek segment of WBI Energy's North Bakken Expansion Project, certificated by FERC in Docket No. CP20-52-000 (application filed Feb. 14, 2020 under NGA section 7(c); EA dated 2021-10-23). The FERC Environmental Assessment's Table A-2 lists five new pipeline facilities matching the five roster rows exactly: Tioga–Elkhorn Creek 62.8 mi/24-in (P3584, this row), Line Section 25 Loop 20.3 mi/12-in (P3585), Line Section 30 Loop 9.6 mi/12-in (P3586), Tioga Compressor Lateral 0.5 mi/20-in (P3587), Elkhorn Creek–Northern Border 0.3 mi/24-in (P3588) — confirmed segment-by-segment, no duplicate/misclassification. It is an interstate NGA section 7(c) transmission certificate (jurisdictional because the project ties into Northern Border's interstate mainline), so 'transmission' classification is correct, not gathering.
SPEC — CONFIRMED with 3 independent sources for this segment specifically (not just the project total): FERC EA (regulatory finding) states 'about 62.8 miles of new 24-inch-diameter natural gas pipeline from new facilities at WBI Energy's Tioga Compressor Station near Tioga...to the proposed Elkhorn Creek Compressor Station...MAOP of 1,480 psig' (p.8). WBI Energy's own project page (operator disclosure) states as 'Key Stats': '62.8 miles of 24-inch diameter natural gas pipeline...Providing up to 250 million cubic feet per day...Starting point: Tioga Compressor Station...End point:...Elkhorn Creek Compressor Station.' NS Energy (independent trade press) separately states 'A 101km-long, 24in-diameter gas pipeline will be constructed from new facilities at the Tioga compressor station...to the new Elkhorn Creek compressor station...MAOP of 1,480 pounds per square inch.' 101 km = 62.77 mi, agrees with 62.8 mi within rounding. All three name this exact segment (not the project total) and agree on length/diameter/pressure. Minot Daily News (construction-start article, Jul. 20 2021) describes the same line loosely as 'about 60 miles of new 20-inch diameter' — a press imprecision (likely conflating this segment's diameter with the 20-in Tioga Compressor Lateral); it does NOT override the three sources that agree exactly and name the segment precisely, so I treat it as expected journalistic rounding, not a real conflict, and did not use it as a corroborating spec source.
CAPACITY 250 MMcf/d ON P3584 IS LEGITIMATE, NOT A COPY-PASTE ARTIFACT — flagging this explicitly since all 5 sibling rows carry the identical 250 MMcf/d and the sweep brief calls that out as a likely aggregate-on-segment defect. For THIS row it is correct: Tioga–Elkhorn Creek is the new mainline trunk between the Tioga Compressor Station (where gas gathered from Line Sections 7/25/30 and the Tioga Gas Plant lateral converges) and the Elkhorn Creek Compressor Station/Northern Border interconnect — i.e. it is downstream of ALL gathering and is the single path the full 250 MMcf/d of incremental firm capacity takes to reach the interconnect. WBI Energy's own page lists 62.8mi/24-in and 'up to 250 MMcf/d' together as this segment's own key stats, and P3588 (the final 0.3-mi Elkhorn Creek–Northern Border tie-in, also downstream of all gathering) legitimately carries the same 250 MMcf/d for the identical reason. By contrast P3585 (Line Section 25 Loop) and P3586 (Line Section 30 Loop) are LOOPS on existing gathering lines upstream of the Tioga Compressor Station, and P3587 (Tioga Compressor Lateral) is a single-plant receipt lateral — none of these three individually carries the full aggregated project capacity, so the same 250 MMcf/d value on those rows is much more likely the aggregate-on-segment defect the brief describes. Recorded as a cross_row_lead below so the fan-out can check P3585/P3586/P3587 specifically; do not treat this note as clearing those rows, and do not treat it as a reason to change P3584's own (correct) value.
OWNER/OPERATOR: sheet's Owner1='WBI Energy' [100%] is correct and current — WBI Energy Transmission, Inc. is the actual FERC applicant/certificate holder (not a stale holding-company name masking the true owner, unlike the Kern River/Santa Fe pattern flagged elsewhere in this batch). NS Energy separately confirms 'WBI Energy, a subsidiary of MDU Resources Group, is the owner and operator.' No attribution concern.
Sources opened: all 4 harvested citations that resolved (FERC EA PDF, NS Energy, WBI Energy project page, Minot Daily News) were read in full; the 5th (Williston Herald) 404s and Wayback returned 429 rate-limit on 2 attempts — not needed since 3 independent sources already corroborate every spec; the 6th (EIA generic 'Natural Gas Data' hub, cite_note-7) is a navigation/data-hub root, not an article naming this pipeline, so it was not cited (per the mutable-navigation-surface rule).

Read the FERC EA for named upstream receipt facilities feeding this segment: it documents SIX processing-plant receipt stations feeding the project's Line Sections 7/25/30 into the Tioga Compressor Station, at least five of which are named — Norse, Lignite, Robinson Lake, Springbrook, and Tioga (the last fed by a dedicated 900-ft, 20-in lateral from Hess Corporation's Tioga Gas Plant). The Tioga–Elkhorn Creek pipeline (this row) is the downstream trunk carrying gas gathered from ALL of these plants combined, not from one specific field/plant, so per the FuelSource convention (name the single upstream field/facility feeding the line; do not default to a generic answer) no single value is honestly attributable here — naming only 'Tioga Gas Plant' would misrepresent the other four contributing plants. cross_row_leads.facts: Line Section 25 Loop: 20.3 mi (6.7 mi Williams Co. + 3.7 mi Mountrail Co. + 10.0 mi Burke Co.), new 12-in-diameter pipeline looping existing Line Section 25 between Tioga Compressor Station and the proposed Norse Transfer Station, bi-directional, MAOP 1,098 psig (upgrading the existing 8-in line's 700 psig). Length/diameter match the sheet exactly. CAUTION: this segment is UPSTREAM of the Tioga Compressor Station (a gathering loop feeding into it, not carrying the full downstream project capacity) — its recorded Capacity=250 MMcf/d is likely an aggregate-on-segment artifact carried over from the project total; worth checking against the FERC EA's per-facility capacity allocation (not stated as a single number per loop in the EA, which is itself evidence 250 MMcf/d may not belong on this row).

Line Section 30 Loop: 9.6 mi, new 12-in-diameter pipeline looping existing Line Section 30 between the existing Nesson Valve Setting and the Tioga Compressor Station in Williams County, bi-directional, MAOP 700 psig. Length/diameter match the sheet exactly. Same caution as P3585: upstream gathering loop, 250 MMcf/d likely not its true segment capacity.

Tioga Compressor Lateral: 0.5 mi, new 20-in-diameter pipeline between the new Tioga Plant Receipt Station and new facilities at the Tioga Compressor Station, MAOP 1,480 psig. This lateral connects specifically to Hess Corporation's Tioga Gas Plant via a separate ~900-ft, 20-in, non-jurisdictional Hess lateral (single-plant receipt point) — length/diameter match the sheet exactly, but as a single-plant receipt lateral it is the least likely of the five segments to legitimately carry the full 250 MMcf/d project-wide capacity figure currently on its row.

Elkhorn Creek–Northern Border pipeline: 0.3 mi, new 24-in-diameter pipeline between the proposed Elkhorn Creek Compressor Station and the new interconnect with Northern Border in McKenzie County, MAOP 1,480 psig. Length/diameter match the sheet exactly. Unlike P3585/P3586/P3587, this segment IS downstream of all gathering (the final tie-in to Northern Border) so 250 MMcf/d is plausibly correct here too, for the same reason it is correct on P3584.

summary: P3584 confirmed real, correctly classified, and every spec (length 62.8mi/24in/1,480psig MAOP, capacity 250 MMcf/d, construction Jul-2021, in-service Feb-2022, ND-ND location, WBI Energy 100% owner/operator) verified against FERC Docket CP20-52-000 + WBI Energy's own project page + NS Energy, all naming this exact segment; FuelSource and SegmentCost left UNRESOLVED (multi-plant aggregation point / project-total-only cost, not fabricated); no existence, duplicate, or classification concerns.
